newsitem.title: USA: Johnston wins Mass. congressional race in recount.
newsitem.headline: Johnston wins Mass. congressional race in recount.

text.p: Philip Johnston has won the battle to become the Democratic nominee for Massachusetts' 10th congressional district - almost.

A recount of the ballots cast in the September 17 primary showed Johnston, a liberal, getting the nomination for the seat 12-term Democrat Jerry Studds is vacating, beating Norfolk County District Attorney William Delahunt by 175 votes, according to the secretary of state.
But Delahunt, who went into the race the presumed favorite, was disputing the results and threatening a lawsuit.

Despite those threats, ballots with Johnston's name and that of his Republican opponent state Rep. Edward Teague, III were ordered printed Monday night, a spokeswoman for Secretary of State William Galvin said.

Teague easily won his nomination capturing some 60 percent of the votes cast in what was the lowest voter turnout in Massachusetts history. Only about 15 percent of eligible voters braved the bad weather to cast their ballots.
First lady Hillary Clinton, who will be making a campaign swing through Massachusetts on Friday, will be stumping for Johnston, a former secretary of human services under then-Gov. Michael Dukakis.
